questions.prompt: Which phrase gives an opinion but shows you're not 100% sure?
questions.explain: “I tend to think” softens your opinion — useful for nuance.

questions.prompt: I'm not ___ convinced that remote work suits everyone.
questions.explain: “Not entirely convinced” = partly doubtful.

questions.prompt: To some ___, I agree with you.
questions.explain: “To some extent / degree” = partly.

questions.prompt: From my ___, the price is the most important thing.
questions.explain: “From my perspective” introduces your personal view.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
questions.explain: Nuanced opinions use softeners, priorities and questions.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: How do you see it?

questions.prompt: Which sentence sounds the most balanced?
options: Social media can be useful, although it depends on how you use it.
questions.explain: Concession (although…) makes an opinion sound balanced.

questions.prompt: “It ___ on the situation.”
questions.explain: It depends on… — note the preposition “on”.

questions.prompt: Which is the most diplomatic way to disagree?
options: I see your point, but I'd look at it differently.
questions.explain: Acknowledge first, then give your view.

questions.prompt: That's a fair argument; ___, I think cost matters more.
questions.explain: “However” introduces a contrasting point.

questions.prompt: I would look at it ___ because I've had a different experience.
questions.explain: Look at it differently = see it another way.

questions.prompt: What ___ you to that view?
questions.explain: “What leads you to that view?” asks for their reasons politely.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
pairs: We may be agreeing more than it seems.
Would it be reasonable to say…?
What leads you to that view?
questions.explain: Diplomatic language keeps a discussion friendly.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: I see your point, but…

questions.prompt: Your colleague says: “We should cancel the project.” A diplomatic reply?
options: That's a fair argument; however, we've already invested a lot.
questions.explain: Acknowledge + however + your reason.

questions.prompt: Which phrase shows partial agreement?
options: I agree up to a point.
questions.explain: “Up to a point” = partly.

questions.prompt: If the train ___ cancelled, we might take a taxi.
questions.explain: “If … were to happen / were” — imaginary future possibility.

questions.prompt: I wouldn't ___ out the possibility of rain.
questions.explain: Rule out = say something is impossible. “I wouldn't rule out…” = it's possible.

questions.prompt: It's quite ___ that the meeting will move online.
questions.explain: It's quite possible/likely that…

questions.prompt: One likely ___ is that the bus was late.
questions.explain: One likely explanation is… — speculating about causes.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to how certain it is.
questions.explain: Modal verbs show how sure you are.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: how likely do you think that is
questions.explain: How likely do you think that is?

questions.prompt: She isn't answering. She ___ be in a meeting.
questions.explain: Might = possible.

questions.prompt: What could ___ the outcome?
questions.explain: We need a verb: influence.

questions.prompt: The delay may be ___ to bad weather.
questions.explain: Due to = because of.

questions.prompt: One ___ could be higher prices.
questions.explain: We need a noun: consequence.

questions.prompt: That tends to ___ to more traffic.
questions.explain: Lead to = cause/result in.

questions.prompt: The main ___ seems to be the cost.
questions.explain: The main factor = the most important cause.

questions.prompt: Match each linker to its meaning.
questions.explain: Linkers help you connect causes and effects.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: What impact would that have?

questions.prompt: More people work from home. ___, there is less traffic in the morning.
questions.explain: As a result introduces an effect.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows a cause?
options: Prices rose because of higher energy costs.
Prices rose, so people bought less.
questions.explain: Because of + cause.

questions.prompt: The ___ of an online course is flexibility.
questions.explain: The advantage of X is…

questions.prompt: The ___ is that it can feel less social.
questions.explain: Drawback = disadvantage.

questions.prompt: In this situation, I would ___ taking the train.
questions.explain: Recommend/suggest + -ing.

questions.prompt: A more ___ option might be to share a car.
questions.explain: A more practical option = a more realistic choice.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
questions.explain: Use these to compare and recommend.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: Which approach seems most effective?

questions.prompt: Which is correct?
options: I recommend to take the bus.
questions.explain: Recommend + -ing (or recommend that you take).

questions.prompt: “It's cheaper, but it's slower.” What's being compared?
questions.explain: Cheaper = advantage, slower = drawback.

sets.title: Discussing change trends and future scenarios

questions.prompt: There has been a noticeable ___ in how people shop.
questions.explain: A shift = a change.

questions.prompt: Online learning is becoming ___ common.
questions.explain: Increasingly + adjective = more and more.

questions.prompt: I expect this to continue ___ prices rise.
questions.explain: Unless = if not.

questions.prompt: In the longer ___, cities may change a lot.
questions.explain: In the longer term / in the long run = in the distant future.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.
pairs: in the future, after some time
questions.explain: Vocabulary for describing trends.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: What trend have you noticed?

questions.prompt: Fewer people buy newspapers. This trend is likely to ___.
questions.explain: Likely to + verb.

questions.prompt: “By 2030, most cars ___ electric.”
questions.explain: Will probably + verb for predictions.

questions.prompt: Before we move on, I'd like to ___ to your earlier point.
questions.explain: Return to = go back to a point.

questions.prompt: That ___ to what you said about cost.
questions.explain: Relate to = be connected with.

questions.prompt: Could we look at this from another ___?
questions.explain: From another angle = from a different point of view.

questions.prompt: The key ___, as I see it, is time.
questions.explain: The key issue = the most important problem.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
pairs: Could we look at this from another angle?
questions.explain: Structure phrases guide a discussion.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: how does that fit with your view
questions.explain: How does that fit with your view?

questions.prompt: Which phrase moves the discussion forward?
options: Shall we consider the budget next?
questions.explain: A clear proposal for the next topic.

questions.prompt: Which phrase shows you're connecting to someone's earlier idea?
options: Going back to what you said earlier…
questions.explain: Going back to… links ideas.

questions.prompt: Could you ___ on what you mean by ‘flexible’?
questions.explain: Expand on = give more detail about.

questions.prompt: If I understand you ___, you're saying that…
questions.explain: We need an adverb: correctly.

questions.prompt: I may not have ___ that clearly.
questions.explain: I may not have expressed that clearly = a polite way to rephrase.

questions.prompt: What I ___ was that we need more time.
questions.explain: What I meant was… — past of mean.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
pairs: Could we distinguish between X and Y?
questions.explain: Clarifying language avoids misunderstandings.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: do you mean that in this context
questions.explain: Do you mean that in this context?

questions.prompt: Someone misunderstood you. Best reply?
options: Sorry, I may not have expressed that clearly. What I meant was…
questions.explain: Take responsibility, then rephrase.

questions.prompt: Which question challenges an idea politely?
options: Could you explain why you think that?
questions.explain: Polite challenge = ask for reasons.

questions.prompt: The ___ reason for this plan is cost.
questions.explain: The strongest reason = the most convincing reason.

questions.prompt: The evidence ___ that people work better in quiet rooms.
questions.explain: The evidence suggests that… (singular subject).

questions.prompt: That ___, we should also consider the risks.
questions.explain: That said = however / despite this.

questions.prompt: For ___, a quiet area helps people concentrate.
questions.explain: For example / For instance introduces evidence.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
questions.explain: A persuasive argument: reason, example, balance.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: how would you support that claim
questions.explain: How would you support that claim?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most persuasive?
options: Studies show that short breaks improve focus, so we should add them.
questions.explain: Evidence + conclusion = persuasive.

questions.prompt: Which word introduces a concession?
questions.explain: Admittedly = I accept this point (before arguing).

questions.prompt: ___ on that, I think we should also look at timing.
questions.explain: Building on that = adding to the previous idea.

questions.prompt: On ___, I think the online option is better.
questions.explain: On balance = after considering everything.

questions.prompt: I'd put it another ___: the problem is time, not money.
questions.explain: I'd put it another way = let me rephrase.

questions.prompt: One possible ___ would be to meet halfway.
questions.explain: Compromise = an agreement where both sides give something.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its function.
questions.explain: Leading phrases help you guide a conversation.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: What should we consider next?

questions.prompt: Two people disagree about the meeting time. Best leading move?
options: One possible compromise would be to meet at 3.
questions.explain: Offer a compromise to move forward.

questions.prompt: Which phrase checks the strongest point?
options: What is the most convincing point?
questions.explain: Asks the group to evaluate arguments.

sets.title: B2 review: nuanced discussion and persuasion

questions.prompt: I see your point, ___ I'd look at it differently.
questions.explain: Polite disagreement: I see your point, but…

questions.prompt: If the price ___ to rise, we might change supplier.
questions.explain: If … were to… — hypothetical.

questions.prompt: The ___ of working from home is flexibility.
questions.explain: The advantage/benefit of…

questions.prompt: On ___, I prefer the second plan.
questions.explain: On balance = overall.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to the lesson skill.
questions.explain: A tour of the main B2 skills.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: that said we should also consider
questions.explain: That said, we should also consider…

questions.prompt: Which sentence explains a consequence?
options: As a result, fewer people drive to work.
questions.explain: As a result → consequence.

questions.prompt: Which is the most diplomatic?
options: That's a fair argument; however, I'm not entirely convinced.
questions.explain: Acknowledge + however + soft doubt.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ inside.
questions.explain: First conditional (real future): if + present, will.

questions.prompt: If I had more time, I ___ learn Japanese.
questions.explain: Second conditional (unreal present): if + past, would.

questions.prompt: If I had known, I ___ you.
questions.explain: Third conditional (past): if + had + pp, would have + pp.

questions.prompt: If I ___ you, I'd accept the offer. (be)
questions.explain: If I were you… (were is preferred).

questions.prompt: We would have caught the train if we ___ left earlier.
questions.explain: Third conditional: if + had + past participle.

questions.prompt: Match the sentence to its meaning.
pairs: If I had won, I'd have travelled.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.
questions.explain: The four most common conditional patterns.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: what would you do if you were me
questions.explain: What would you do if you were me?

questions.prompt: Which is correct?
options: If I would know, I would tell you.
If I knew, I would tell you.
questions.explain: No “would” in the if-clause: If I knew…

questions.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
questions.explain: Although + clause (subject + verb).

questions.prompt: ___ the rain, we went for a walk.
questions.explain: Despite + noun.

questions.prompt: It was raining. ___, we went for a walk.
questions.explain: However starts a new sentence, followed by a comma.

questions.prompt: In spite ___ the traffic, we arrived on time.
questions.explain: In spite of = despite.

questions.prompt: Despite ___ (feel) tired, she finished the report.
questions.explain: Despite + -ing.

questions.prompt: Match each linker to how it's used.
pairs: at the start of a new sentence
questions.explain: Contrast linkers follow different patterns.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: we enjoyed it despite the cold
despite the cold we enjoyed it
questions.explain: We enjoyed it despite the cold.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Despite it was late, we stayed.
Although it was late, we stayed.
questions.explain: Although + clause; despite cannot be followed by a clause.

questions.prompt: Can we ___ a decision today?
questions.explain: Make a decision (take a decision is also used in British English).

questions.prompt: I'd like to ___ a point.
questions.explain: Raise a point = bring up an idea.

questions.prompt: Let's ___ an agreement.
questions.explain: Reach an agreement.

questions.prompt: She ___ a good argument.
questions.explain: Make an argument.

questions.prompt: We need to take this ___ account.
questions.explain: Take into account = consider.

questions.prompt: I see it from a different point of ___.
questions.explain: Point of view = perspective.

questions.prompt: Match the verb to its collocation.
questions.explain: Strong collocations make your English sound natural.

questions.prompt: Which collocation is correct?
questions.explain: We make mistakes.

questions.prompt: The report ___ by the manager yesterday.
questions.explain: Past passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.prompt: A new office ___ next year.
questions.explain: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.prompt: It ___ that prices will rise.
questions.explain: It is expected that… — reporting without naming who.

questions.prompt: The decision has ___ made. (be)
questions.explain: Present perfect passive: has been + pp.

questions.prompt: He is said ___ be a great speaker.
questions.explain: Be said to + verb.

questions.prompt: Match the active to the passive.
pairs: He is said to be rich.
questions.explain: Passive puts the focus on the action, not the person.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: The meeting has been cancelled.

questions.prompt: When is the passive most useful?
options: When who did it is unknown or unimportant
When you want to sound informal
questions.explain: We use the passive when the action matters more than the person.
